In the Olympic Peninsula of northwest Washington State, a small town named Forks exists under a near-constant cover of clouds. It rains on this inconsequential town more than any other place in the United States of America. It was from this town and its gloomy, omnipresent shade that my mother escaped with me when I was only a few months old. It was in this town that I'd been compelled to spend a month every summer until I was fourteen. That was the year I finally put my foot down; these past three summers, my dad, Charlie, vacationed with me in California for two weeks instead. I loved Phoenix. I loved the sun and the blistering heat. I loved the vigorous, sprawling city.

(I'm sorry) There was this Cheerio. He was a nice cheerio, with a simple life. He went to work every day at the frosting company, went to the bar every night, and went home and went to bed to start over again the next morning. However, one day after work, he saw this fine lady cheerio, and it was love at first sight. He went up to the lady cheerio, slightly intoxicated, and said, "hey baby, wanna head out for a night on the town?" The lady cheerio made a face of disgust, looked him up and down and said, "eww, no, you're not frosty enough. Get frosted and come back, maybe I'll give you a chance."

So he went home, disappointed, and slumped into bed. When he awoke, he had an idea. He rushed to get ready for work and drove faster to work than he normally did. When he got into work, he immediately paged his boss and asked for a meeting. His boss obliged and the cheerio went into his boss's office.

"Hey boss, I need you do to a favor for me." "No problem for one of my hardest working employees! What do you need?" "I need to get frosted by tonight."

His boss made a frown of concern. "Getting frosted can have serious adverse effects. If you want me to do this, you'll have to sign this waver." And, like any other intelligent working-class cheerio would do to woo a fine lady cheerio, he signed the waver without reading even a word, and went into the frosting chamber. He only had enough money to get 25% frosted, so that's all he did. He was sure it would be enough.

That evening after work, he went to the bar and waited to see if the lady cheerio would come. After about 30 minutes of waiting, he heard the door open and a pair of heels click into the bar. He quickly turned, and was ecstatic to see his lady cheerio had arrived! He walked up to her confidently and said, "notice anything different?"

The lady cheerio made a face of confusion, because she didn't remember this strange man, and then remembered him from the night before. She again looked him up and down, and made a smirk. "Nice try, honey, but that's not enough for me." His heart sank as she walked towards the bar to order a drink, ignoring him. He went home without getting a drink that night with a plan.

The next morning, he called into work and said he'd be a bit late. He took his new plasma flat screen TV that he had spent 4 months saving for, went to the pawn shop, and pawned it off for enough money to get more frosting. He went into work and scheduled another appointment with his boss.

This time, his boss seemed to know what he was there for before he came in. "Son, I don't know if you want to do this," said his boss with a raised eyebrow. "Getting 50% frosted can seriously damage you for life." But the cheerio was filled with infatuation, and signed the waver without speaking to the boss. He gave his boss the money, and entered the chamber.

Once again he rushed to the bar, ready to woo his lady. When she got there shortly after he did, he shuffled up to her, slightly more nervous this time, and stuttered, "how's this?"

She looked annoyed, and that made him back down a little bit. "Come back to me when you're COMPLETELY frosted, then we'll talk." He was crushed. He didn't have that kind of money! But he knew, this lady was the right one for him. That night, before he went home, he went to the bank and got a loan. He had a spotless credit score, and had been loyal to this bank for twenty years, so they gave him a loan with a low interest rate, with little negotiation.

He came in early to work, before his co-workers were there, so he could talk to his boss right away. He exploded into his boss's office and shouted, "I NEED TO GET 100% FROSTED," knowing full well that this would decrease his lifespan by at least 10 years. His boss sighed, and looked disappointed. It was sad to see such a hard-working and good cheerio be destroyed by a selfish lady-cheerio gold-digging at a bar. Yet, the cheerio's life was not his business. He got out a waver for the third time and told the workers to fire up the frosting chamber early.

That night, he ran to the bar, since he was legally not allowed to drive less than 32 hours after becoming 100% frosted. The lady cheerio was already there by the time he arrived. She turned, saw him, and smiled a devilish grin. "That's what I'm looking for," she purred. He felt the butterflies in his stomach take off. He stuck out his frosty arm for her to take hold of, flagged down a taxi, and prepared for a night of fun.

Near the end of the night, they ended up at a bar. They were both tired, and looking for a drink. The lady cheerio asked the frosted cheerio, "Can you go wait in the beer line and grab us a few?" He happily obliged, and waited in the beer line with his remaining loan money. However, when he got to the front, they were all out of beer! They didn't get a restock until the next week, and they hadn't been expecting as many guests as they'd had that night. He went back and told her. "Fine," she groaned, "grab us some wine." So he went to the wine line, a little worried about his funds at this point, as the wine was slightly more expensive. To both his relief and dismay, they were out of wine as well. He went back to his lady and told her this and she groaned loudly. "Fine, just see if you can find us some punch."

So he went to look for the punch line, but there wasn't one.
